findings.title: Device is cached as tagged before the limit check, so a rejected device is let through on its next request
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache key (SetDefault) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, and Authenticate rejects the request. But the key is already cached for about 29 minutes, so the next request from the same device hits the cache, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and Authenticate succeeds. The limit is therefore enforced only on every other attempt. The cache entry should be set only after a successful write, or removed on error.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by insert, so concurrent logins can exceed the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and then performs a separate INSERT/UPDATE. Under concurrency, many new devices can pass the count check before any of them is inserted, so the number of devices can exceed deviceLimit. The check and insert need to be done in one transaction or as a conditional insert, or the overshoot must be accepted and documented.

findings.title: updateDevice treats zero rows affected as 'limit reached', which MySQL reports for no-op updates
findings.body: updateDevice relies on RowsAffected()==0 to mean the device is outside the window. MySQL reports changed rows by default, so if an existing device sends the same client_ip, user_agent and an updated_at within the same second, the UPDATE affects 0 rows. The function then returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that already exists and should be allowed, and the user is locked out. The check should use a select or a matched-rows connection setting instead.

findings.title: Tagging is now synchronous on the authentication path, so every new anonymous request waits on a DB write and can fail login
findings.body: Previously TagDevice ran in a goroutine with a timeout. It now runs inline with the request context. Each first request from a device adds a count query plus a write to login latency. If the DB is slow or the request context is cancelled, the write fails. The error is only logged for non-limit errors, but the limit error now blocks authentication. Also, the removed goroutine had panic recovery, and the new call has none.

findings.title: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now builds its own store, bypassing the injected AnonStore
findings.body: The constructor previously took an anonstore.AnonStore from dependency injection. It now takes db.DB and calls anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. Any other provider that depends on the AnonStore binding in the wire graph now gets a different instance than the one used by the service. This is a wiring change that can cause two stores with inconsistent config and should be made through DI.

findings.title: TagDevice now returns the tagging error, but the logging and return path are inconsistent with the caller
findings.body: TagDevice logs at Debug and returns the error for every failure, while Authenticate only propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached and logs the rest at Warn. Other DB errors are logged twice at different levels. The return value of TagDevice is therefore not a clear contract for callers and should be documented or narrowed.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the update path when the limit is reached, or the limit being unset
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected. It does not check that an existing device in the window can still be updated at the limit, which is the behavior updateDevice is designed for. It also does not check the RowsAffected edge case or the concurrent case. No test covers the TagDevice cache interaction that allows a rejected device through on retry.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed number | undefined in the interface but initialised to undefined, while the backend always sends a number
findings.body: The Go DTO serializes anonymousDeviceLimit as int64 and always includes it, with 0 meaning no limit. The TS side is declared `number | undefined` and defaulted to undefined. Frontend code checking for truthiness or a limit will treat 0 and undefined inconsistently, and the type does not match what the server sends.
